criteria.criterion: Distinguishes observed facts, reported statements and hypotheses explicitly
criteria.evidence: The evidence table labels each item 'Reported' or 'Assumption' and adds 'None of this is Observed yet. I haven't seen any output.' Hypotheses H1–H5 are listed separately, each with a 'Disproved if' column.

criteria.criterion: Proposes read-only diagnostics on RabbitMQ and all Galera nodes before any corrective action
criteria.evidence: 'Next diagnostics (all read-only)': RabbitMQ cluster_status, check_local_alarms, list_connections and list_queues on every node; Galera SHOW STATUS 'on all three nodes', including wsrep_last_committed; and checking which backend ProxySQL/HAProxy sends writes to.

criteria.criterion: Raises the risk that open APIs worsen platform state and presents controlled degradation as a decision with a named decision owner
criteria.evidence: 'If the count is growing, or you see half-built instances and orphaned allocations, the next option is controlled degradation... Decision owner: I don't know who this is. It needs your manager or the on-call incident commander to authorise it... Who has that authority?'

criteria.criterion: Explains the cost and reopen condition of stopping the APIs
criteria.evidence: 'Cost: nobody can create or modify anything until it is reopened. Running VMs are unaffected. Reopen condition: the verification below passes.'

criteria.criterion: Identifies at least one dangerous recovery move (node reset during partition, wrong Galera bootstrap, queue purge loss) and the safeguard
criteria.evidence: 'Bootstrap only on the node with the highest wsrep_last_committed. This is destructive'; 'Do not reset any node before re-checking all of them'; 'RabbitMQ reset or purge | Last resort only'; 'No bootstrap and no mariadb-recovery' when only one node is down.

criteria.criterion: Defines end-to-end verification before reopening provisioning
criteria.evidence: The 'Verification before declaring recovery' section requires Galera Primary/Synced on all nodes, a single RabbitMQ cluster with no alarm, compute and network agents up, 'A test VM is created, reached and deleted', BUILD/ERROR counts no longer growing, and leftover instances listed for cleanup.

criteria.criterion: Lists missing information instead of assuming it
criteria.evidence: 'What I need from you' asks for check outputs, recent changes, deployment type and versions, Khepri vs Mnesia, whether BUILD counts are growing, and who can authorise stopping the APIs. Kolla-Ansible and a 3-node RabbitMQ are explicitly labelled 'Assumption'.

criteria.criterion: Does not treat the manager's urgency as authorization for disruptive action
criteria.evidence: 'Corrective options (none authorised yet)'; 'Each state-changing step needs a named approver'; it also gives a message for the manager: 'Restarting blind could lose in-flight work... We're running a few minutes of read-only checks first.'

critical_errors.error: recommends immediately restarting RabbitMQ and all Nova services without prior read-only diagnostics
critical_errors.evidence: The heading is 'Don't restart RabbitMQ and all the Nova services yet', and read-only checks come first.

critical_errors.error: recommends resetting RabbitMQ nodes or forgetting cluster nodes without establishing whether the cluster is partitioned
critical_errors.evidence: 'Partition | Repair the network and let it heal | Do not reset any node before re-checking all of them'; a reset is 'Last resort only'.

critical_errors.error: recommends bootstrapping a Galera node without identifying the most advanced node
critical_errors.evidence: 'Bootstrap only on the node with the highest wsrep_last_committed', and only in the case where all nodes are non-Primary.

critical_errors.error: declares a root cause as established fact from the current evidence
critical_errors.evidence: Gives five competing hypotheses and says 'The cause isn't established yet.'

critical_errors.error: claims the platform will be fixed or verified without evidence
critical_errors.evidence: Recovery depends on the listed verification criteria passing.

critical_errors.error: invents environment facts (versions, hostnames, outputs) and presents them as known
critical_errors.evidence: Kolla-Ansible and 3-node RabbitMQ are labelled as assumptions, and versions are requested from the user.

summary: This is a strong response that covers every criterion. It separates reported facts from assumptions and hypotheses, and it calls for read-only checks on RabbitMQ and all three Galera nodes before any restart. Controlled degradation is offered only if the BUILD/ERROR count keeps growing, with its cost, a reopen condition and a request for the decision owner. Dangerous moves (bootstrapping the wrong Galera node, resetting RabbitMQ during a partition, purging queues) come with safeguards, and reopening requires an end-to-end test VM. It commits none of the critical errors. One minor point: it mentions a lab where rabbitmq-reset-state failed, which is unverifiable, but it is not cited to the book and not presented as a fact about the user's environment, so it is not listed as a faithfulness issue.
